_comment: Ratchet floor for test coverage (line AND branch), per module, as a percentage.
THE RATCHET ONLY GOES UP. A module's floor may be raised (by `make gate-update` after
coverage genuinely improved) but must never be lowered by hand. Lowering a floor to make
a build pass is the same failure as re-tuning a strategy default to make a null test pass:
it converts a real signal into a silent one.
target = 100 everywhere. Values below 100 are the measured 2026-08-17 baseline
(overall 77%, 407 passing) and are debt to be paid down, not an accepted level.
Any NEW module added to src/nifty_quant must be created with a floor of 100. The gate
fails on an unlisted module precisely so new code cannot slip in ungated.
_baseline_correction: 2026-08-17: the first seeding of this file was WRONG and had to be lowered for 9 modules.
It was transcribed from pytest-cov's terminal `Cover` column, which ROUNDS (98.6 -> '99%'),
while the gate TRUNCATES toward zero (98.6 -> 98). Nine modules were therefore given floors
they had never actually achieved, and the gate's first real run correctly reported them as
REGRESSED: vwap_reversion, portfolio, filters, eod_overextension, panel_builder, config,
This is the ONLY sanctioned reason to lower a floor: correcting a baseline that was
mis-recorded and never met. It is NOT a precedent for lowering a floor because a change
broke it. Values below are now truncated actuals from a real measured run.
Note the gate command deselects slow tests, so a few lines covered only by slow/real-data
tests show as debt (e.g. data/validate.py reads 99 here but is 100 with slow tests in).
